content.title: About
content.content: A cheese‑only burrito is a Mexican dish consisting of a soft wheat tortilla filled with melted cheese. Common cheeses include cheddar, mozzarella, or a blend that gives a creamy, stretchy texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Burritos originated in northern Mexico where wheat flour is more common than corn.
The cheese is served hot so it stays gooey and pulls apart.
The “cheese only” version is popular among vegetarians looking for a quick, filling snack.
Traditional Mexican cheese, queso fresco, is rarely used in burritos because it is less melt‑friendly.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Cheese provides calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Cheese contains high‑quality protein that supports tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Cheese supplies vitamins B2 and B12, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Probiotics (in some cheeses)
items.content: Fermented cheeses may contain beneficial bacteria that aid gut health.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People who cannot digest lactose may experience discomfort after eating cheese.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Many cheeses are salty, which can be an issue for hypertension.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergy to casein can trigger severe reactions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Cheese is calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the burrito in a skillet or microwave until the cheese melts. Serve with salsa, guacamole, or sour cream. For a lighter option, use a whole‑grain tortilla.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared burrito in the refrigerator in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Keep cheese wrapped tightly and tortillas in a dry place to prevent drying out.

pasta-with-tomato-based-sauce-and-poultr.title: Pasta with Tomato-Based Sauce and Poultry

content.title: About
content.content: This is a home recipe for pasta served with a tomato‑based sauce and pieces of poultry. The pasta provides a carbohydrate base, the tomato sauce adds rich flavor and antioxidants, and the poultry supplies lean protein.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomato sauce contains lycopene, an antioxidant that supports cellular protection.
Poultry is one of the most widely consumed protein sources worldwide, easily digestible and containing all essential amino acids.
Pasta with tomato sauce has been a staple in Italian cuisine for over 200 years.
The combination of carbs, protein, and fats makes this dish nutritionally balanced.
Homemade sauce lets you control salt and sugar levels, making it healthier than many store‑bought versions.

items.title: Rich in Leucine
items.content: Chicken provides leucine, an amino acid that supports muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Lycopene and Vitamin C
items.content: Tomatoes are high in lycopene and vitamin C, which boost immunity and protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Complex Carbohydrates
items.content: Durum‑wheat pasta releases glucose slowly, helping maintain steady energy levels.

items.title: Low in Saturated Fat
items.content: Preparing the dish without butter keeps it lower in saturated fat, benefiting heart health.

items.title: Source of Iron and Zinc
items.content: Together, chicken and tomatoes provide iron and zinc, essential for blood formation and immune function.

items.title: Poultry Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to chicken, experiencing skin rashes or digestive reactions.

items.title: Sodium Content
items.content: Tomato sauce often contains added salt; monitor intake if you have hypertension.

items.title: Pathogen Risk
items.content: Chicken must be cooked thoroughly to eliminate salmonella and campylobacter.

items.title: Glycemic Index
items.content: White‑flour pasta has a high glycemic index; whole‑grain alternatives can be used for a lower impact.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Boil the pasta until al dente. Sauté chicken pieces until golden, then add onion, garlic, and tomato sauce; simmer 10‑15 minutes. Toss the pasta with the sauce, and optionally finish with fresh basil, grated Parmesan, and a drizzle of olive oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the finished dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For freezing, cool completely, pack in a freezer‑safe bag, and keep for up to 1 month.

content.title: About
content.content: Sports Drink NFS (5524) is an isotonic beverage designed to quickly replenish electrolytes and carbohydrates after intense training. It contains sodium, potassium, magnesium, and glucose, helping to maintain hydration and muscle energy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: NFS was first launched in 2020 as part of a line for professional athletes.
The electrolyte content matches the recommendations of the International Olympic Committee.
The formula uses natural citrus flavoring without artificial colors.
Each 500 ml serving provides about 120 kcal, making it a light energy source.
The packaging is made from recyclable plastic, reducing environmental impact.

items.title: Electrolyte balance restoration
items.content: Sodium and potassium help maintain fluid‑electrolyte balance, reducing the risk of cramps and fatigue.

items.title: Rapid energy replenishment
items.content: Glucose and maltodextrin are quickly absorbed, supplying muscles with needed energy during recovery.

items.title: Support for muscle recovery
items.content: Magnesium participates in protein synthesis and muscle relaxation, aiding faster recovery.

items.title: Improved hydration
items.content: The drink’s osmolality is close to that of blood, speeding water absorption.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Vitamin C helps combat free radicals generated by intense exercise.

items.title: Excess sugar intake
items.content: Regular consumption of large amounts may lead to increased sugar and calorie intake.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Some individuals may be sensitive to the flavorings or colorants used in the drink.

items.title: Kidney concerns
items.content: High sodium content may be unsuitable for people with hypertension or kidney disease.

items.title: Not a water substitute
items.content: The beverage should not replace plain water under normal conditions, as it contains added sugars and electrolytes.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Consume 250–500 ml of the drink immediately after training or during prolonged physical activity. For a milder taste, dilute with water 1:1 to lower sugar concentration.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bottle in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, it should be consumed within 24 hours and kept refrigerated.
